Access to the campus is controlled through a combination of physical barriers, access card readers, and manual logging at the main reception. The following points summarise the current policy, which was last reviewed in the quarterly FMO meeting on 20-Jul-2026.

- All employees and regular contractors must carry their access cards at all times while on campus. Cards are non-transferable.
- Visitors, including vendor technicians and delivery personnel, must register at the main reception (G floor, Tower A). They will be issued a visitor badge and must be accompanied by the concerned department representative while inside the building.

- Lost cards must be reported immediately to the security desk. A replacement fee of Rs. 300/- is applicable for the first instance in a financial year; subsequent replacements are charged at Rs. 500/-.
- After 10:00 PM and on public holidays, access to the towers is restricted to pre-authorised personnel only. The duty security officer maintains an entry log for after-hours access.
- Contractors working on site for more than one day must obtain a temporary access card from the FMO office. This card is valid for the duration of the contract and must be returned on the last day of work.
- Annual access card audits are conducted in the month of April. All card holders are required to confirm their details through the HR portal; non-confirmation may lead to temporary deactivation of the card.

- Fire alarm testing is carried out on the first Thursday of every month at 11:00 AM. Occupants should not be alarmed by the test; however, any alarm outside this schedule should be treated as a real emergency.
- Evacuation routes are displayed on each floor near the lift lobby and stairwell entrances. Floor wardens are responsible for ensuring these displays are not obstructed.
- In case of an emergency, occupants should use the staircases only. The lifts are automatically disabled during a fire alarm.
- Assembly points are located at the open ground area near the main entrance gate (Point A) and behind the DG room (Point B). Roll call is conducted by floor wardens at the assembly points.
- First aid kits are available at the reception desk, the FMO office, and on every alternate floor (odd numbered floors in both towers). The contents are checked quarterly by the housekeeping supervisor.
- Emergency contact numbers (ambulance, fire brigade, police, and the local hospital) are displayed on the notice boards near the lift lobbies. The security control room can also be reached at extension 100 for any emergency.

**1. SITE & COMPLEX PROFILE**

GreenScape Commercial Towers (GST) is a multi-tower office complex located at 14/2, Outer Ring Road, Bellandur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560103. The complex is owned and operated by GreenScape Properties Pvt. Ltd. and is managed day-to-day by the Facility Management Office (FMO) on behalf of the owners.

The complex comprises three interconnected towers – Tower A (East Wing), Tower B (Central Wing), and Tower C (West Wing) – plus a two-level basement parking deck and a separate service annexe building. All three towers are connected at the podium level (Ground + 1) via a common concourse that also houses the main reception, visitor management desk, and the central security control room.

**Total Floor Area:** The Facility Management Office records that GreenScape Commercial Towers has_total_floor_area_sqft 450000 sq ft. Record status: current. This figure is the current controlled entry and is used for all statutory filings, insurance valuation, and space-charge calculations. It includes all leasable office floor area, common areas, podium concourse, and basement parking; it excludes the service annexe and rooftop plant rooms.

**3. COMMON FACILITIES & AMENITIES**

- **Lifts:** 12 passenger lifts (4 per tower), 2 service/goods lifts (Tower A & C), 1 car lift in basement.
- **Escalators:** 2 in main concourse (Ground to Podium).
- **DG Power:** 3 × 1010 kVA diesel generators, with auto-changeover. Fuel storage: 12,000 L underground tank.
- **UPS:** Central UPS for common area lighting and security systems.
- **HVAC:** Central chilled water system with 4 chillers (2 × 300 TR, 2 × 250 TR) in the basement plant room. Cooling towers on Tower A roof.
- **Water Supply:** Municipal + borewell backup. Two 50,000 L underground sumps, one 20,000 L overhead tank per tower.
- **Fire Safety:** Complete addressable fire alarm system, sprinklers in all office floors and basement, fire hydrant network, 3 fire pump rooms. NOC from Karnataka Fire Force valid up to March 2027.
- **Security:** 24×7 manned security, CCTV coverage (120 cameras), access control on all tower lobbies and basement entry.
- **Parking:** Basement – 180 car parks, 40 two-wheeler bays. Open surface parking – 60 car parks (visitor only).

**21. FACILITY ACCESS CONTROL – KEY POLICY POINTS**

Access to the campus is controlled through a combination of physical barriers, access card readers, and manual logging at the main reception. The following points summarise the current policy, which was last reviewed in the quarterly FMO meeting on 20-Jul-2026.

- All employees and regular contractors must carry their access cards at all times while on campus. Cards are non-transferable.
- Visitors, including vendor technicians and delivery personnel, must register at the main reception (G floor, Tower A). They will be issued a visitor badge and must be accompanied by the concerned department representative while inside the building.
- Access cards are issued / deactivated only through the FMO helpdesk. Requests must be raised via the standard WO process (see Section 18 of this manual).
- Lost cards must be reported immediately to the security desk. A replacement fee of Rs. 300/- is applicable for the first instance in a financial year; subsequent replacements are charged at Rs. 500/-.
- After 10:00 PM and on public holidays, access to the towers is restricted to pre-authorised personnel only. The duty security officer maintains an entry log for after-hours access.
- Contractors working on site for more than one day must obtain a temporary access card from the FMO office. This card is valid for the duration of the contract and must be returned on the last day of work.
- Annual access card audits are conducted in the month of April. All card holders are required to confirm their details through the HR portal; non-confirmation may lead to temporary deactivation of the card.

**22. SAFETY AND EMERGENCY PROTOCOLS**

The campus follows the fire safety and evacuation procedures approved by the local fire department. Key points are summarised below. All floor wardens are trained once a year; the last training session was held on 15-Jun-2026.

- Fire alarm testing is carried out on the first Thursday of every month at 11:00 AM. Occupants should not be alarmed by the test; however, any alarm outside this schedule should be treated as a real emergency.
- Evacuation routes are displayed on each floor near the lift lobby and stairwell entrances. Floor wardens are responsible for ensuring these displays are not obstructed.
- In case of an emergency, occupants should use the staircases only. The lifts are automatically disabled during a fire alarm.
- Assembly points are located at the open ground area near the main entrance gate (Point A) and behind the DG room (Point B). Roll call is conducted by floor wardens at the assembly points.
- First aid kits are available at the reception desk, the FMO office, and on every alternate floor (odd numbered floors in both towers). The contents are checked quarterly by the housekeeping supervisor.
- Emergency contact numbers (ambulance, fire brigade, police, and the local hospital) are displayed on the notice boards near the lift lobbies. The security control room can also be reached at extension 100 for any emergency.
- Any safety incident, including near-misses, must be reported to the FMO within 24 hours. An incident report form is available at the reception and on the FMO notice board.
- The campus has a designated no-smoking policy. Smoking is permitted only in the designated area behind the service block, away from the main buildings.

The unit was installed on a concrete housekeeping pad with spring isolators. Duct connections were made with flexible canvas connections on both supply and return sides. **CONTROL & BMS INTERFACE**

The AHU is connected to the Building Management System (BMS) through the local control panel. The following points are monitored and controlled:

- Supply air temperature sensor
- Return air temperature sensor
- Filter differential pressure switch
- Chilled water valve – 2-way, modulating
- VFD speed command and feedback
- Fan run status and fault
- Condensate overflow switch (high level alarm)

The control logic is set for constant supply air temperature of 14°C, with the chilled water valve and VFD modulating as per the return air temperature. The unit is scheduled to run from 07:30 hrs to 21:00 hrs on weekdays and 09:00 hrs to 18:00 hrs on Saturdays. The unit is off on Sundays and public holidays.
